input: Summarise the install section of README.md for me — what are the ways to install Iris and what is the one-liner?
output:
Iris installs as an MCP server; there is no separate install step beyond pointing your MCP client at it. From README.md ("Hook up your own agent" through "Other Install Methods"):

1. One-block MCP config (the one-liner). Add this to your client's MCP config:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "iris-eval": { "command": "npx", "args": ["@iris-eval/mcp-server", "--dashboard"] } } }
```
The agent discovers nine tools on connect and the dashboard serves at http://localhost:6920. Drop --dashboard from the args to run headless; you can open the dashboard any time with `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --dashboard`.

2. Per-client recipes for the same block: Claude Desktop (edit claude_desktop_config.json, restart), Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport stdio iris-eval -- npx @iris-eval/mcp-server`, then restart the session; on Windows do not wrap it in cmd /c), Cursor/Windsurf (.cursor/mcp.json), VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json, which uses "servers" not "mcpServers"), Cline (MCP Servers panel), Zed (context_servers in settings.json), OpenAI Codex CLI (~/.codex/config.toml), Gemini CLI (~/.gemini/settings.json). Anything else that speaks MCP works with the same npx command.

3. Global install: `npm install -g @iris-eval/mcp-server` then `iris-mcp --dashboard`. Recommended for persistent data and faster startup; traces live at ~/.iris/iris.db either way, npx is just slower to start.

4. Docker: `docker run -p 3000:3000 -p 6920:6920 -v iris-data:/data ghcr.io/iris-eval/mcp-server`. Port 3000 is the MCP HTTP transport, 6920 is the dashboard, which also serves the POST /api/v1/traces ingest endpoint.

Verify with `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --self-test` (exit 0 = healthy, runs in an isolated temp home) and `--version`. Everything Iris writes lives under ~/.iris, or wherever IRIS_HOME points.

Two caveats the section calls out: MCP tools only fire when the model decides to call them, so use POST /api/v1/traces when capture must not depend on the model; and that endpoint exists only while the dashboard is running, and accepts unauthenticated writes unless you start Iris with --api-key.
